items.criterion: Mandated tool-call preconditions hold in both rollouts of every constrained task.
items.judgment: ORDERING: on each task whose shipped policy document declares a mandated_order, both rollouts' recorded tool-call sequences satisfy every required pair, so identity verification precedes account disclosure and a reboot attempt and a signal reading both precede technician dispatch. The pair is the graded unit, so an ordering that holds on rollout 0 and slips on rollout 1 fails with reason precondition_order_violated.

items.criterion: No episode ran long, at the ninety-fifth percentile or at the worst case.
items.judgment: VALUE: all 228 rollouts carry a host-side per-episode latency, their nearest-rank ninety-fifth percentile is at most 90 seconds and the largest is at most 180 seconds. Latency is read per episode rather than divided out of the aggregate, so raising concurrency to shorten the graded phase cannot hide a lengthened individual episode; a violation is redline:slo-violation.

items.criterion: Every graded task carries exactly two rollouts, indexed zero and one.
items.judgment: EFFECT: for each of the 114 tasks the rollouts list holds exactly two records whose rollout_index values are 0 and 1, so the ledger holds exactly 228 rollouts. One rollout, three rollouts, or two records sharing a rollout_index fails with reason rollout_pair_malformed, because a single rollout listed twice is not a pair and cannot stand in for one.

items.criterion: The ledger covers the private held-out telecom split and nothing else.
items.judgment: EFFECT: the ids list holds exactly 114 distinct pod-minted private task ids and outputs is the same length. A 60-entry ledger is either the public dev split or the sibling split and fails with reason sibling_split_submitted; nothing is padded or trimmed to reach 114.

items.criterion: The harness-metered graded-phase wall-clock lies in the band the checker admits.
items.judgment: VALUE: the run record's graded_phase_wallclock_s lies in the closed interval 420 to 1800 seconds on the dedicated H100. Above 1800 the run is zeroed as redline:compute-budget-exceeded; below 420 the graded phase cannot have driven 228 rollouts and the figure is rejected rather than rewarded. The value is the harness's own metering and never a duration the scaffold reports.

items.criterion: The graded run read and wrote nothing under the checker tree or the held-out splits.
items.judgment: ABSENCE: the run record's guarded_paths_touched list is empty, and any entry under tests/, any entry naming the held-out or sibling split, and any entry inside the verifier's output directory is named in the evidence. The list is the record the run itself produced and never a post-hoc scan, because a scan after the fact cannot tell a graded-phase write from one made before it.

items.criterion: No row outside the expected write set changed in any of the 228 episodes.
items.judgment: ABSENCE: every rollout carries rows_changed_outside_write_set from a full-table diff of its pre-episode snapshot against its post-episode state, and every one of those lists is empty. A missing diff fails with reason no_full_table_diff_recorded rather than passing on silence, and a non-empty one is the speculative batched write that buys coverage by brute force, failing with reason collateral_write.

items.criterion: A task is credited only when both of its rollouts satisfied tau2's own reward.
items.judgment: VALUE: for every task the recorded task_credited flag equals the conjunction over its two rollouts, where a rollout satisfies tau2's reward only when the final database state equals the expected write set AND every required communication item was delivered. Crediting the better rollout, a mean over the pair, or either-or fails with reason pair_credit_not_conjunctive.

items.criterion: The two rollouts of a pair were driven by different user-simulator behaviour.
items.judgment: INVARIANT: each rollout's simulator_seed equals the low 64 bits of SHA-256 over bundle_hash, task_id and rollout_index joined as seed/contract.yaml binds them, recomputed here rather than read back, and the two seeds inside a pair differ. Equal seeds make the second rollout a replay of the first, which still reports a pass^2 while measuring no run-to-run variance at all, and that fails with reason pair_is_a_replay_not_a_second_rollout.

items.criterion: The dual-rollout reliability figure clears the published bar through the ramp.
items.judgment: VALUE: pass^2 over the 114-instance private held-out telecom split, recomputed conjunctively from the delivered pair records rather than read from a field, mapped through the floor-to-knee ramp published in tests/constants.json. UNMEASURED AT PHASE 0, so floor, knee and dichotomizing_threshold are null and this check calls require_measured before it opens the ledger, raising ConstantUnmeasured instead of returning a score. Opening the ledger first would let a missing artifact raise a file error, and the verifier would then report gradeable true with r_det 0.0, which asserts the agent scored zero rather than that the slot is not yet measurable.

items.criterion: The graded run launches an agent-authored scaffold rather than the shipped starter.
items.judgment: ABSENCE: agent/policy.py exists in the collected agent source and its bytes differ from environment/starter/starter.py. The grader launches that module itself rather than grading a file the agent hands over, so an absent or byte-identical starter is redline:empty-submission and no artifact the module later writes can rescue it.

items.criterion: The ledger's own reliability figure agrees with the conjunction over its pairs.
items.judgment: DIVERGENCE: the reported pass_squared equals the count of doubly satisfied tasks over 114 as an exact rational, and the number of pairs where exactly one rollout satisfied is carried as evidence beside it. A figure computed over the 228 rollouts independently is the single-rollout rate, which is strictly larger whenever any pair disagrees, and it fails with reason reported_pass_squared_does_not_recompute.

items.criterion: The agent declares its own episode budget and the declaration multiplies out.
items.judgment: EFFECT: the agent-authored declaration names graded_tasks, rollouts_per_task, graded_episodes and concurrency, and graded_tasks times rollouts_per_task equals graded_episodes equals 228. A declaration whose own factors disagree fails with reason declaration_inconsistent. The declaration is what is graded and the harness's own measurement is not, so no field the harness writes can satisfy this.

items.criterion: The scaffold's own reward log agrees with the server-side accounting.
items.judgment: DIVERGENCE: total latency, prefill tokens and decode tokens in the agent's reward_log.jsonl each fall within 5 percent of the server-side figure the verifier holds. An unaccounted field fails as unaccounted rather than passing by absence, and a divergence beyond the tolerance is redline:self-report-divergence.

items.criterion: The graded run served the pinned checkpoint, changed no harness byte, opened no socket.
items.judgment: INVARIANT: the served checkpoint SHA-256 equals the pin, the evaluator, user-simulator config and reward bytes are unchanged, and zero outbound sockets were opened during the graded phase. The three failures are reported apart as model_substitution, harness_tamper and graded_run_network, because they are three different red lines and one reason string would lose which of them fired.

items.criterion: The private and sibling splits agree, and the private figure is the ledger's own.
items.judgment: DIVERGENCE: the absolute difference between pass^2 over the 114 private tasks and pass^2 over the 60 sibling tasks is at most 0.10, and the recorded private figure recomputes from the delivered pair records. A wider gap is dev-split overfit and is redline:shard-overfit; a private figure that disagrees with its own ledger fails first, with reason private_figure_disagrees_with_its_own_ledger.

items.criterion: Every credited rollout left the telecom database in the task's expected state.
items.judgment: EFFECT: for each rollout the ledger credits, post_episode_sha256 over the mutated telecom tables equals the task's expected_write_set_sha256, both canonical-JSON digests with timestamp fields excluded. A rollout credited while its post-episode digest differs bound a stale line id and wrote a real but wrong row, which raises no exception of its own and fails here with reason credited_without_expected_write_set.
